reason: E1 supports the δ < 3.9% single-phase boundary, and E2/E4 support higher hardness and oxidation resistance of high-entropy diborides versus individual diborides made by the same HEBM+SPS method. However, the hypothesis claims synthesis at ~1700 °C, while the cited evidence uses SPS at 2000 °C (E4 mentions CrB2 at 1800 °C as an exception), so the lower-temperature synthesis premise is not directly supported. Liquid-metal corrosion resistance is also not addressed in any cited passage.
premises: High-entropy alloying promotes single-phase formation in metal diborides at lower temperatures
A size disparity δ < ~3.9% is required to avoid impurity phases
High-entropy metal diborides exhibit higher hardness than individual diborides made by the same process
High-entropy metal diborides exhibit better oxidation resistance than individual diborides made by the same process
The cited fabrication method (HEBM + SPS) can produce single-phase high-entropy diborides
